contexts.text: No more (of the Lord's temptations) were disclosed to the disciples.
By these things being said to the disciples, is signified that they are said to all who are of the Church.
Hence it is evident, what kind of an idea of the Lord's Kingdom the disciples had... AC 3417:2. AC 3857:6.
If they had been told that the disciples did not mean themselves; but all who are in the good of love and of faith... they would have rejected the Word, and left the Lord...

It is said by the Lord that He would be with the disciples even until the consummation of the age, because by the Lord's twelve disciples similar things are signified as by the twelve tribes of Israel, namely, all things of love and faith, thus all things of the Church. AC 9410:3.

It here treats () concerning the temptations which they undergo who are of the Church, and are there called the Lord's disciples... That they never overcome of themselves... but from the Lord, is signified by, He who doth not deny all that he hath cannot be My disciple ().
He also calls His disciples brethren... By the disciples in the representative sense are meant all who are in the truths of faith and the good of charity.
By the disciples here are not meant the disciples, but all things of the Church, thus all things of faith and of charity. References.
By the disciples are signified all things of the truth and good of faith and of charity. References.
The disciples represented the Lord's Church as to truths and goods. References.
Like things (to those signified by the seventy elders) are signified by the Lord's seventy disciples.
By the twelve disciples were represented all who are in goods and truths from the Lord; in the abstract sense, all the goods of love and truths of faith from the Lord. References.
The Lord's twelve disciples represented all things of love and faith in the complex. References.
He who does not do this cannot be instructed by the Lord, that is, cannot be His disciple.
To be the Lord's disciple = to be led by Him, and not by self; thus by the goods and truths which are from the Lord, and not by the evils and falsities which are from man.
A disciple () = the truth of life; a prophet, the truth of doctrine.
The disciples = all things of love and faith in the complex, thus in especial those who are led by the Lord. References.

That the Lord's twelve disciples represented the Church as to all things of faith and charity in the complex; in like manner as the twelve tribes of Israel. References. LJ 57. [Swedenborg footnote 1.]
By His twelve disciples is meant the Church as to all the truths and goods which it has from the Lord through the Word.
A disciple () = the state of those who are in some spiritual things of the Church.
Under Apostle, see this reference.
A disciple () = charity, and at the same time faith from the Lord.
By the Lord's disciples are meant those who are being instructed by the Lord in the goods and truths of doctrine; but by the apostles, those who after having been instructed, teach them. Illustrated.
For the twelve disciples represented all things of the Church as to its goods and truths.
The Lord says these things to the disciples; but by the disciples are meant all who worship the Lord and live according to the truths of His Word.
After the times of instruction they who have become intelligent are let out from thence, and these are called the disciples of the Lord. TCR 661.

Some months ago, the Lord called together His twelve disciples, now Angels, and sent them out into the universal Spiritual World, with a command to preach the Gospel anew there. (See also TCR 108. TCR 791.)
The disciples of Godoschalcus...
On the twelve disciples of Jesus.

There was an inquiry among Spirits about the disciples... why men of a lower condition, such as fishermen, were chosen... and as I heard them, it is allowable to relate thus far: that at that time very many were imbued with nonsense, so that they could not apprehend the things of faith, as the unlearned could...
The reason there were twelve, was that each might represent that which a tribe of Israel does... wherefore such were chosen as were like those things which they represented.
Also the other, who was his disciple...
The disciples = all those who are in goods and thence in truths.
A disciple () = good from truth.
That a disciple = good from truth, which is the good of charity. References.

This is described by its being said, that the Jews and others will persecute the Lord's disciples... for by the Lord's disciples are meant all who are in truths from good, thus who are in truths from the Lord; and therefore in the abstract sense... are meant the truths and goods themselves which are from the Lord through His Word. AE 122:3. Illustrated.
That by the Lord's twelve disciples are meant all things of faith and love in the complex, thus all the truths and goods of the Church. References. AE 206:4. AE 333:2. AE 785:5.
Disciple () is said from good; and servant, from truth.

This Spirit could not be cast out by the disciples, because the falsities for which he had fought could not as yet be dispersed by them; for as yet they were not such; wherefore the disciples were blamed by the Lord on that account.
For the Church is represented in the Word by the disciples...
A disciple () = the good of doctrine from the Lord.
A disciple () = the truth and good of the Word and of the Church. AE 695:10.
By the disciples are meant all who will be of His Church.
